# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates and multi-period population series for 4.123 individually assessed settlements across 17 West African and Sahelian countries between 1880AD and 1975AD, encompassing 22.108 archival observations. Screened from 6.392 candidate towns, colonial stations, ports and metropolitan agglomerations (2.269 excluded), the retained entries span fourteen colonial territorial sub-regions across French West Africa, British West Africa, Togoland, Portuguese Guinea and Liberia. Active interpolated series expand from 68 towns in 1880AD to 3.109 in 1900AD, 3.872 in 1930AD, 1.820 in 1950AD and 519 by 1970AD, tracing urban development from early port settlements to metropolitan Lagos (1,49M), Abidjan (951,2k), Ibadan (768k), Accra (624,1k), Dakar (591k) and Kano (390k).



# Background

Colonial rule across West Africa and the Sahel transformed urban hierarchies built during the precolonial savanna and forest eras [@Services2013WritingHistory; @Ittmann2010DemographicsEmpire]. While older overland caravan centres such as Timbuktu, Saint-Louis and Kong grew modestly or stagnated, deep-water Atlantic ports and railway junctions - Dakar, Abidjan, Lagos, Port Harcourt, Accra, Takoradi, Conakry, Lomé and Cotonou - expanded rapidly as colonial fiscal systems channelled groundnuts, cocoa, palm produce and mineral exports toward ocean shipping [@AOFAnnuaire1936; @Manchuelle1997WillingMigrants; @Adjepong2013StrangersAnd]. Compiling these enumerations into one unified settlement ledger illuminates how transport geography and post-1945 public health campaigns shifted demographic gravity toward the coast [@Vrooman2025TheColonial; @Faye2021WaterResources].

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Territorial Assignment

Candidate settlements were assembled from colonial decennial censuses in Nigeria, the Gold Coast, Sierra Leone and The Gambia [@Kuczynski1948DemographicSurvey1; @Cardinall1932GoldCoast; @Office1951AnnualReport], five-year federal enumerations in French West Africa [@AOFAnnuaire1936], Portuguese Guinea and Liberian administrative records, and post-1950 national statistical yearbooks [@Akinyoade2017CensusTaking]. From 6.392 candidates within the 6.050.194 km² study perimeter bounded by geoBoundaries polygons [@Runfola2020GeoBoundaries], 2.269 duplicate orthographies and non-settlement fragments were excluded across four screening waves, retaining 4.123 entries (4.068 city-proper and 55 metropolitan agglomerations). Each settlement is assigned deterministically to its historical colonial territory among the 14 sub-regions, placing Nigerian Western Region towns (including Ibadan, Abeokuta, Ogbomosho and Oyo) in Southern Nigeria, Ilorin and Benue-Plateau towns in Northern Nigeria, and nine Cameroon-Chad frontier towns in the adjoining Nigerian colonial zones.

## Interpolation and Scope Conventions

Where colonial or national censuses provide multi-year series, Tables 1 to 14 report linearly interpolated populations at six chapter benchmarks (1880AD, 1900AD, 1930AD, 1950AD, 1960AD and 1970AD) alongside each entry's peak population and peak date, marking years outside the documented observation span with a hyphen (-). Post-1950 metropolitan agglomerations are retained alongside city-proper municipal counts and labelled explicitly with "(Agglomeration)" so urban corridor expansion can be tracked without conflating municipal and peri-urban boundaries [@Faye2021WaterResources].

# Testing and Validation

Across all 4.123 individually assessed entries, upper-tier rank-size regression ($n = 180$) yields a Zipf exponent of $q = 0,93$ ($R^2 = 0,98$), while the 679 spatially deduplicated towns plotted in Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank} yield $q = 0,88$ ($R^2 = 0,99$), confirming consistent multi-port urban scaling across French, British, German, Portuguese and Liberian territories [@FrankemaJerven2014AfricanPop; @Akinyoade2017CensusTaking].

## AOF: French Sudan (Soudan Français)

# Limitations

Three caveats govern this settlement ledger. First, 207 of the 4.123 settlements hold single-date observations, meaning benchmark columns display a hyphen outside their recorded census or survey span. Second, early colonial records under-counted dispersed rural towns across interior protectorates relative to coastal municipal ports [@Kuczynski1948DemographicSurvey1; @Services2013WritingHistory]. Third, 55 post-1950 metropolitan agglomerations sit alongside municipal city-proper records for the same capitals and should not be summed mechanically without separating spatial scopes [@Akinyoade2017CensusTaking; @Faye2021WaterResources].

# Conclusion

Taken together, these 4.123 individually assessed settlements document the urban transformation of West Africa and the Sahel between 1880AD and 1975AD, tracing the expansion of colonial railway towns, port capitals and cash-crop market hubs from Dakar and Bathurst to Lagos and Kano.
